Combine palettes: one color from each of a set of colorways

Source: R/palettes.R
glyos_combine.Rd

Takes one color from each named palette, or from every palette of a company or product line, and returns them as a single categorical palette named by the colorway each color came from. This is the quick way to get "one color per Kabuto Mushi" or "one color per Battle Tribes figure".

Usage

glyos_combine(
  palettes = NULL,
  company = NULL,
  line = NULL,
  which = 1L,
  distinct = FALSE
)

Arguments

palettes

Character vector of palette names; see glyos_palette_names(). May be omitted when company or line is given.

company, line

Optional filters passed to glyos_palette_names(); every matching palette contributes one color.

which

Which color to take from each palette (1 is the main plastic color). Palettes with fewer colors contribute their last one.

distinct

Logical. Choose each palette's contribution to be as different as possible from those already chosen, instead of position which?

Value

A named character vector of hex colors with class "glyos_palette", one per palette, in the order of palettes or of glyos_palette_names(). Pass unname()d to ggplot2::scale_colour_manual().

Details

By default the first color of each palette is used, which is the main plastic color and so is faithful to each figure but can repeat across a line cast from shared plastics. distinct = TRUE instead picks, for each palette in turn, the color from that palette that is farthest (in CIE Lab) from the colors already chosen, which keeps the result legible on a chart at some cost to fidelity. For a stricter selection that also drops colors with poor contrast against the background, see glyos_pick().

See also

glyos_pick(), glyos_palette()

Examples

glyos_combine(c("standard", "spectre", "hades", "infection", "glyaxia"))
#> Glyos combined palette 'standard + spectre + hades + infection + glyaxia' (5 colors)
#> standard = #8ED7EE
#> spectre = #EEFADA
#> hades = #0F1210
#> infection = #D00615
#> glyaxia = #F2B61D

glyos_combine(line = "Kabuto Mushi")
#> Glyos combined palette 'kabuto mushi' (10 colors)
#> kabuto_standard = #B29E5B
#> kabuto_infection = #E61B11
#> kabuto_radioactive = #1BC46A
#> kabuto_glyaxia_clone = #0885F2
#> kabuto_scarabite = #1698CF
#> kabuto_xenoglow = #5CD432
#> kabuto_cerulestar = #99C2C5
#> kabuto_bioberry = #1753A5
#> kabuto_luna = #8FBDCE
#> kabuto_sectivorus_supreme = #C4A679

glyos_combine(line = "Kabuto Mushi", distinct = TRUE)
#> Glyos combined palette 'kabuto mushi' (10 colors)
#> kabuto_standard = #B29E5B
#> kabuto_infection = #E61B11
#> kabuto_radioactive = #F54C9C
#> kabuto_glyaxia_clone = #0885F2
#> kabuto_scarabite = #0A1114
#> kabuto_xenoglow = #5CD432
#> kabuto_cerulestar = #648F99
#> kabuto_bioberry = #09286B
#> kabuto_luna = #A71F17
#> kabuto_sectivorus_supreme = #7E634C

glyos_combine(company = "Toyfinity", which = 2)
#> Glyos combined palette 'toyfinity' (12 colors)
#> rf_maxx_zero = #242123
#> rf_hun_dred = #B9C3BE
#> rf_sentinel = #E6BA0F
#> rf_wrecker = #91AB54
#> rf_vanguard = #0A5178
#> rf_cruel = #34167D
#> rf_brutal = #C00633
#> rf_nazgar = #65451F
#> mordles_jumbo = #F55B43
#> zeroids_zerak = #051C41
#> zeroids_zobor = #DEA793
#> manglors_manglord = #A8B46F


library(ggplot2)
ggplot(mpg, aes(displ, hwy, color = drv)) +
  geom_point(size = 2.5) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = unname(glyos_combine(c("glyaxia", "hades", "infection"))))
